recommendation_issues.problem: Choosing MAS-L2 pulls in identity pinning: MASWE-0028 'Insecure Identity Pinning' carries profiles [L2, EUDIW] and maps to MASVS-NETWORK-2. That collides with the automatically renewed certificate of S05-02, and on Android the pins live in the native network security config, so a broken pin cannot be fixed by an over-the-air update; offline records would pile up on phones until a new APK is installed. The plan's real threat (students tampering with the app, emulators) maps to L1 plus R (plus P); pinning should be declared out of scope, or done on a stable key with a backup pin. The target should also name MASTG v2 and MASWE v1, where the profiles now live, not only MASVS 2.1.0.

Dropping @fastify/cors is a net removal only if a front (Caddy from S05-02 or an İÜ gateway) serves panel and API on one origin; otherwise Fastify needs @fastify/static, a swap rather than a removal. It also makes the panel rely on the CORS preflight, and ASVS 5.0 3.5.2 (L1) then requires that no sensitive call works through a non-preflighted request, while Fastify parses text/plain by default. This change must ship together with the Origin check from the line 598 miss.

Advisory tracking is handed entirely to Dependabot alerts, but with pnpm 11 and 12 lockfiles Dependabot reported zero dependencies and closed alerts without an update until a fix shipped on 2026-09-07, and GitHub's docs still list pnpm v7 to v10 only. The recommendation needs the one-time check and the 'pnpm audit' second signal from the line 720 miss, plus the count correction above.

A device-keyed limit is safe only after the device is verified. @fastify/rate-limit attaches to onRequest by default, before any auth hook, so the device-keyed limits need hook 'preHandler' registered after the step that verifies the device; a device id taken from an unverified header can be rotated per request to dodge the limit. Eviction from the 5000-entry LRU makes the limiter forget clients (it fails open), so the table size is about protection, not about false 429s.

Compose file secrets satisfy ASVS 13.3.2 (per-service least privilege) but are plain files on the host, so they do not by themselves meet 13.3.1 ('a secrets management solution, such as a key vault'). Adding a vault for one server would be bloat; the plan should record the remaining 13.3.1 gap instead of implying full L2.

The instance table and getInstances() exist only since pg-boss 12.36.0 (published 2026-10-02), so the plan must pin at least that version for this check, and nothing in the plan reads the table or raises an alert from it (line 714 miss on restart and alerting).

misses.finding: API, worker and PostgreSQL share one host and no memory limits are set. PostgreSQL's docs warn that the kernel OOM killer can terminate the postmaster when another process exhausts memory, which would take the database down for every service. Compose offers mem_limit (and oom_score_adj) per service, so a runaway Node process dies inside its own container instead.

evidence.quote: the kernel might terminate the PostgreSQL postmaster (the supervisor server process) if the memory demands of either PostgreSQL or another process cause the system to run out of virtual memory.
evidence.date: PostgreSQL 18 docs, Linux Memory Overcommit, accessed 2026-10-05

evidence.quote: configures a limit on the amount of memory a container can allocate, set as a string expressing a byte value.

misses.recommendation_tr: API ve işçiye Compose'da bellek sınırı (mem_limit) konur ve under-pressure'ın bellek eşiği bu sınırın altında seçilir. Böylece belleği taşan bir Node süreci makinedeki PostgreSQL'i değil yalnız kendi kabını düşürür.
